## 2025/26 - year at a glance

- Overall, we received 214,600 new complaints in 2025/26
- This is an almost 30% decrease compared to the 305,700 complaints we received in 2024/25
- On average, across all financial products, we upheld 30% of the complaints we resolved

## Trends across the year in financial products

Overall this year, we received 214,600 complaints about financial products and services.

This is closer to the number of complaints received in 2023/24, following a year of significant demand in 2024/25.

Hire purchase (motor) was the most complained about product this year with 37,700 complaints received, with many of those received in the first half of the year. The total number of complaints about Hire Purchase (Motor) for the year was lower than last year, when we received 76,200 complaints.

There were 32,900 complaints about current accounts, with fraud and scams accounting for 18,900 of these cases.

Credit cards were the third most complained about product, with around 22,800 complaints, 8,800 of which were about perceived irresponsible/unaffordable lending. This is a significant drop on the 49,400 new credit card complaints on irresponsible/unaffordable lending referred to us in 2024/25.

Percentage - top 5 most complained-about products

## Complaints brought by professional representatives

Last year, we introduced charges for professional representatives to refer cases to our service to make our funding arrangements fairer and to encourage professional representatives to submit better-evidenced complaints, considering their merits more diligently before referring them to us.

Since then, we’ve seen a drop in cases brought to us by professional representatives. Cases from professional representatives made up 18% of our caseload in 2025/26, with 38,600 cases referred to us. In 2024/25, complaints brought by professional representatives made up 50% of our caseload (152,800 cases). We've also seen a drop in complaints being withdrawn or abandoned once they come to us, from 35% in 2024/25 to 18% in 2025/26.
